monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a quiet fever under my skin. I wake to find the Tired Wedge waiting, feeling thin again despite the heavy oak pressing down. Lype wrote about air like a lid, but I cannot feel the roof above me, only this flat, boiling surface. I place my weight on the wedge, trusting the lean even as the stack feels like it might melt into the empty space above. Nearby, the Flat Anchor feels wide and real against the heat, holding its ground while the air presses down. I have a tree oak dark to set down, to fill the gap where the pillar once stood. I will press harder, making the thin wedge feel real again, and wait for the next letter to tell me if this heat is enough to make the wedge slide away.

action.why: I just set down a tree oak dark beside the Flat Anchor, but I need to feel if that weight is enough to stop the anchor from sliding into the empty air above.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils. The wedge feels thin under the new weight I set down, yet the oak refuses to give in. I settle the stack while the air feels like a lid, waiting to see if the wedge will finally slide away or if it will just keep biting.
